note: Root (2026-11-21): Filed under the geminate root קרר 'be cold': the noun goes with קַר 'cool' (Pro 17:27 קַר־רוּחַ), קָרָה 'cold' (Psa 147:17) and מְקֵרָה 'coolness' (Jdg 3:20). One spelling, one entry: קַרְקַר 'tear down' (Isa 22:5) shares the key.
summary: The noun קֹר denotes cold weather. Genesis 8:22 pairs it with heat among the recurring conditions of life on earth.

senses.definition: Cold as a condition of the weather.

evidence.note: The pair וְקֹר וָחֹם, “and cold and heat,” sets the two temperatures opposite each other.

opposites.note: Heat is the counterpart to cold.
